title: Post-labeling cleanup cheat-sheet and heuristics (personal notes)
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal reference for post-labeling cleanup passes. Target: small, deterministic auto-fixes + triage signals for human review. Meant to be run after first-pass labels and before eval set freeze.

High-level checklist (order matters):
1) Run label-consistency validator (exists: scripts/label_lint.py) -> capture: span-overlaps, nested mislabeled, label-empty spans.
2) Tokenization alignment pass: align labels to tokenizer output (BPE/byte-level). If >3% tokens misaligned, flag dataset for re-tokenize/re-annotate.
3) Canonicalize punctuation & whitespace (rules below).
4) Apply deterministic regex-based fixes for high-precision patterns (emails, GUIDs, ISO dates).
5) Sample-level spot-checks: stratified by label frequency + long-tail tokens + high model-disagreement.
6) Auto-fix where confidence >= 0.99 AND rule is high precision; otherwise add to human-review queue.

Common heuristics and why they matter:
- Merge punctuation-only spans: labels like "ORG" applied to "," or "." are almost always junk; remove if span is only punctuation and label frequency < 0.1%.
- Trim leading/trailing whitespace inside spans: annotators sometimes include a leading space when dragging; normalize to exact character spans.
- Prefer longest-safe span for overlapping entity types if the shorter span is a substring and label same type (e.g., 'San Francisco' vs 'San'). Keep longer, but flag exceptions for acronyms.
- Date normalization: convert locale-ambiguous dates (01/02/2023) to ISO-8601 in an aux column; keep original span but add normalized_date field for downstream tasks.
- Numeric ranges: unify formatted numbers (1,000 vs 1000) for aggregator features; keep raw text for model inputs.

Tokenizer-specific notes:
- If tokenizer splits tokens inside annotated span boundaries (subtokenization), create subtoken-to-char mapping and map labels to first subtoken. But record original char-span.
- For byte-level tokenizers: when a span boundary falls mid-byte-sequence, prefer expanding to adjacent whitespace boundary unless it changes semantics.

Edge-cases + quick examples (BEFORE -> AFTER):
1) Email-like but not email (single @ used as separator):
   BEFORE: "username@ domain" labeled EMAIL
   AFTER: change to LABEL_NONE; add note 'space after @' to review list

2) URLs with tracking params:
   BEFORE: span = 'https://example.com/?utm=123' LABEL=URL
   AFTER: canonicalize to 'https://example.com/' in aux_canonical_url, keep original span and LABEL=URL

3) Code snippets mistaken for identifiers:
   BEFORE: 'fn calculate_sum(arr: &Vec<i32>)' labeled as FUNCTION_NAME on 'calculate_sum'
   AFTER: keep label but add label_attr 'source=code' and don't count towards named-entity metrics

4) Hyphenation across lines (OCR artifacts):
   BEFORE: 'high-
performance' labeled as single ADJ span
   AFTER: merge into 'high-performance' and mark as 'ocr_fix'

Deterministic regex suggestions (high-precision rules to run early):
- Email:  [A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,} 
- ISO Date:  \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} 
- GUID:  [0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12} 
- URL (simple): https?://[^\s/$.?#].[^\s]*
Note: keep conservative; false positives cascade. Document each applied regex in audit column.

Auto-fix policy (rules to follow):
- Allow auto-fix if (rule_precision_estimate >= 0.995) AND (dataset_frequency_of_apply >= 0.0001).
- Otherwise, add to 'candidate-fixes.csv' with sample_count=50 for manual review.

Sampling & QA strategy:
- Stratify samples by: label_freq_quartile, avg_span_length_bucket, tokenizer_mismatch_flag, model_confidence_bucket.
- For each stratum pick min(10, 0.01 * stratum_size) random samples + top 5 highest-disagreement examples.
- Record per-sample disposition: keep / change / unclear. Track why (short note).

Metrics to track (post-cleanup):
- % spans trimmed/expanded
- % regex-applied auto-fixes and manual revert rate
- Tokenizer-mismatch rate pre/post pass
- Inter-annotator agreement on sampled re-annotations

Quick fixes & scripts to run (notes for future cleanup automation):
- lightweight aligner: scripts/char_align.py --use-bpe-map
- postprocess pipeline: scripts/postlabel_pipeline.sh => lint -> align -> regex-fix -> dedupe -> sample-export
- adb: export candidate-fixes.csv to label-studio for focused review batches

Open questions / follow-ups:
- When to prefer removing a span vs marking as LABEL_NONE? (Tradeoff: model recall vs dataset cleanliness.)
- How to represent canonical forms without breaking original text fidelity in training? (aux columns vs replaced tokens)
- Edge-case policy for nested person/company tokens in product names.

TODOs (my personal next steps):
- Add a small notebook that measures misalignment rate across tokenizers we use (hf-roberta, tiktoken, byte-level).
- Create 'high-precision regex' registry with one-line justification + sample false positives.
- Export candidate-fixes to label-studio, set up a 2-hour triage session with Meera.

Notes-to-self: keep aggressive auto-fix thresholds strict; easy to introduce systemic label noise. Prefer auditability (audit column + rule id) over silent fixes.

End of notes.
